messages.author: 4fb76301a14d098f
messages.subject: Using Subjunc for Arabidopsis
parts:
I have been using Subjunc for several SRA runs downloaded from NCBI. So far the default has given high mapped rates. My questions are partially due the compact nature of Arabidopsis genome as well as prior experiences from other aligners. Any feedback would be appreciated.
  1. <-n> Several libraries have very short reads (36 bp). When I aligned short-read library by TopHat, I often get high multiple alignment rates (offered by TopHat’s align summary). Since the read length of subheads is 16 bp, I wonder if I need to modify <-n> according to the read length.
  2. Intron size. For Arabidopsis, the min/max intron size I tend to use is 50/2000. This would be very different from mammal genomes. So I wonder if  there’s a option for this.
  3. <-M> Since the mismatch is not allowed for subhead, what does -M apply to?
  4. <-d/-D> The meaning of these options changed in earlier version, so is the fragment/template length equivalent to mate inner distance? If not, is there an argument for that purpose?

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Using Subjunc for Arabidopsis
parts: <-n> Several libraries have very short reads (36 bp). When I aligned short-read library by TopHat, I often get high multiple alignment rates (offered by TopHat’s align summary). Since the read length of subheads is 16 bp, I wonder if I need to modify <-n> according to the read length.

If the default setting was used when you built the index (subread-buildindex command), subreads will be extracted from the reference genome in every three bases, ie. there is a 2-bp gap between each pair of neighbouring subreads. When using this index for alignment, you can only extract up to 7 subreads from a 36bp read ((36-15)/3). Subjunc by default tries to extract 14 subreads from each read. When there are less than 14 subreads available, it will extract as many as it can. For a 36bp read, it will extract 7 subreads which is the maximum number. So you do not need to modify -n. Subjunc takes into account the read length when it extracts subreads.

Another option you may try is to build a full index, ie subreads are extracted from every position of the reference genome. This will enable more subreads to be extracted for very short reads and it may further improve the mapping results. You can use the following command to build a full index:

subread-buildindex -F -B -f 72 -o subread_fullindex your_reference_genome.fasta
Intron size. For Arabidopsis, the min/max intron size I tend to use is 50/2000. This would be very different from mammal genomes. So I wonder if  there’s a option for this.

We do not have a specific option for this. But I believe the current options should work well for your data. Subjunc requires the presence of donor and receptor sites when calling exon-exon junctions, so it should be pretty accurate for mapping your Arabidopsis data. It also favors shorter introns when a read can be best mapped to both a short intron and a long intron.
Since the mismatch is not allowed for subhead, what does -M apply to?
-M is applied to the comparison between the entire read sequence and the target sequence. More specifically, it applies to the regions in a read which were not covered by the mapped subreads.
<-d/-D> The meaning of these options changed in earlier version, so is the fragment/template length equivalent to mate inner distance? If not, is there an argument for that purpose?

-d/-D specifies the range of the lengths allowed for templates. It is not for the mate inner distance. You can actually set -d/-D values to get your required mate inner distance. For example, if your reads are 100bp long, you can set the minimum fragment length to be 250 to require the minimum mate inner distance to be 50.

Thank you for the detailed explanation. I just have a follow-up question.

If -M applies to the max mismatches allowed in a read, should I adjust it according to the read length? Is up to 10 mismatches for a 36- or 50-bp read too high?

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Using Subjunc for Arabidopsis
parts: Yes, I think you should adjust it. The default value of -M has been changed to 3, but you may choose to use 1 or 2 for 50bp reads.
